dimension_rule: A non-null ref means the dimension applies; null means not applicable. A ref is covered only if it resolves to a numbered section that explicitly cites the requirement ID.

requirements.title: Backend is a Python Flask modular monolith exposing a versioned REST API.
Internal application frontend is built with Lit and TypeScript and deployed separately from the marketing site.
Backend API is deployed on AWS, independently of Cloudflare Pages.
All data access goes through SQLAlchemy; business code contains no engine-specific SQL, so SQLite to PostgreSQL requires no application changes.
All schema changes are versioned Alembic migrations; no manual DDL in any environment.
Every module, PR and test references requirement IDs.
Timestamps are stored in UTC and displayed in the user's timezone (default Asia/Kolkata).
Configuration comes from the environment; no secrets in the repository.
Business reference lists are configurable lookup data, not code enums.
Human-readable record numbers are allocated from a central sequence table and are internal display values only.
A module accesses another module only through its service interface, never its tables or repositories.
Roadmap modules (vendor, inventory, payroll, procurement, full project management and others in doc 10) are not authorized for implementation in P0.
The User entity's physical table is app_user; no physical table named user may exist.
Every persisted table includes the nine audit-contract columns; deviations are behavioral only and registered.
id is UUIDv7 as 32 lowercase hex characters, generated in the service layer, immutable.
created_on and updated_on are NOT NULL UTC values set by the platform from one transaction clock reading.
created_by and updated_by are NOT NULL foreign keys to app_user.id; non-human writes use seeded system users.
Soft delete via is_deleted, deleted_on, deleted_by with a consistency constraint.
Optimistic concurrency via version; stale updates are rejected.
Business-key uniqueness applies only among non-deleted rows (partial unique indexes).
Default reads exclude soft-deleted rows; including them requires explicit opt-in and permission.
Business records are never hard-deleted outside retention, erasure or registered exceptions.
Foreign keys are enforced by the database on every engine.
A schema conformance check on SQLite and PostgreSQL fails CI on any contract violation.
GUID maps to CHAR(32) on SQLite and native uuid on PostgreSQL; every foreign key uses the GUID type; all type mappings are explicit.
Malformed ids are rejected with 422 INVALID_ID; integer ids and sequence values are never exposed as identifiers.
Behavioral exceptions to the contract are listed in an exception registry; unregistered deviations fail CI.
Contract fields, audit rows and outbox rows are written in the same database transaction as the business change.
Money is stored as integer minor units with an ISO currency code.
Every create, update, soft-delete, restore and hard-delete of an audited entity writes an audit_log row in the same transaction.
Audit rows capture entity_type, entity_id, action, old_value, new_value, performed_by, performed_on.
Audit rows also capture changed_fields, request_id, transaction_id, performed_via, ip_address, user_agent.
audit_log is append-only, enforced by the database.
Secret fields are never written to audit payloads.
Child-entity changes record their parent so parent history includes children.
Bulk exports are audited (who, when, filter, row count).
Audit Log Viewer with filters by entity, actor, action, date, gated by audit.read.
Configurable audit retention with verified archival.
A write without an actor context fails (fail closed).
Personal-data anonymization of audit payloads only via an audited procedure.
Authentication and security events are recorded in security_event_log, never in audit_log.
Tamper-evidence hash chain over audit_log.
Users sign in with email and password.
Passwords are hashed with Argon2id and rehashed when parameters strengthen.
Password policy: 12 to 128 characters, blocklist, no composition rules.
Access token is a 15-minute ES256 JWT held in memory only.
Opaque refresh token rotated on every use in an HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie; reuse revokes the session.
Sessions are persisted server-side and revocable immediately.
Logout ends the current session; logout-all ends every session.
Forgot and reset password with a single-use, 30-minute, hashed token delivered by email.
Login and forgot-password responses do not reveal account existence.
Brute-force protection: account lockout, per-IP and edge rate limits.
No self-registration; staff accounts are invited.
Users can change their password; other sessions are revoked.
All authentication events, including every token refresh, are recorded in security_event_log.
The first Founder is created by a one-time CLI bootstrap; no default credentials exist.
MFA is enforced according to the MFA policy (ADR-006).
Users list and revoke their sessions; admins revoke any user's sessions.
Deactivating or deleting a user revokes all their sessions immediately.
Initial personas Founder, Admin and Sales are supported.
A dedicated append-only security_event_log exists, separate from audit_log.
The event catalog covers login, refresh, logout, session revocation, password reset, MFA enrollment and challenges, lockout, permission-sensitive actions and blocked intake.
No raw or hashed tokens, passwords, OTP secrets or codes, recovery codes or request bodies are stored; detail keys are allow-listed.
Retention is configurable, and rows are archived with verification before deletion.
Access is controlled by security_event.read with ALL and OWN scope; there is no write API.
Tamper evidence: DB immutability, hash chain and nightly verification.
The daily chain head is anchored in S3 Object Lock.
Indexed, cursor-paginated queries by time, subject, type, IP and outcome.
Monitoring and alerting rules for security events.
Capacity figures are assumptions until measured; review after 30 days of production traffic.
Failure and denial events persist even when the triggering request rolls back.
TOTP authenticator-app MFA with enrollment and login challenge.
MFA is mandatory for Founder and Admin through data-driven policy (role.mfa_required), never role-name checks.
MFA is configurable for Sales per user (app_user.mfa_required) or per role.
Holders of any sensitive permission must use MFA.
Ten one-time recovery codes, shown once, stored only as keyed hashes.
MFA enrollment, challenges, recovery-code use, regeneration and resets are security events.
MFA reset only through a privileged, step-up, reason-required, audited workflow with no self-reset and no stronger target.
No security questions, SMS/email OTP factors or device-remember bypass.
TOTP replay protection and attempt limits.
TOTP secrets are KMS-envelope-encrypted and never returned after enrollment.
Step-up MFA within 10 minutes for sensitive operations.
Tables app_user, role, permission, user_role, role_permission, user_permission exist before any business module.
Authorization checks permission codes only; no role-name, is-admin or user-id checks.
Permission codes follow the resource.action convention.
Permissions are declared in a code registry and synchronized by migration.
Each grant carries a data scope: ALL, TEAM (reserved) or OWN.
Direct user GRANT and DENY; DENY always wins.
Role and permission assignments can be time-bound.
Founder, Admin and Sales roles are seeded with the default matrix.
Anti-escalation: an actor cannot grant permissions or scopes they do not hold.
Users cannot modify their own roles or permissions.
Changes that would leave no active administrator are refused.
Enforcement at route, service and query layers; UI checks are cosmetic.
Authorization changes take effect on the next request via authz_version.
A record outside the actor's scope returns 404.
System roles and permissions cannot be deleted; their codes are immutable.
An effective-permissions view explains every permission's source.
Sensitive permissions need a reason and step-up to grant, emit SENSITIVE_ACTION events on use and require MFA of holders.
Authorized users can invite, read, update, deactivate and soft-delete users.
User status lifecycle INVITED, ACTIVE, LOCKED, DISABLED.
Email is unique case-insensitively among non-deleted users.
Users can view and edit their own profile.
Seeded non-login system users SYSTEM, WEB_INTAKE and ANONYMOUS exist.
User management shows MFA status and offers MFA administration.
The website enquiry form creates leads through a public API endpoint.
A lead holds name, phone, email, city, project_type, budget_range and message plus the audit contract.
Authorized staff can create leads manually.
Lead status is NEW, CONTACTED, SITE_VISIT, QUOTATION_SENT, NEGOTIATION, WON or LOST.
Status changes follow the state machine; illegal transitions are rejected.
LOST requires a lost reason; WON records won_on.
Leads can be assigned to users who hold lead.read.
Each lead has a unique internal number VS-L-YYYY-NNNNNN, never shown publicly.
Phone numbers are validated and normalized to E.164 with India as the default region, accepting international numbers with a country code.
Likely duplicates are flagged and never rejected or silently discarded.
Source and campaign attribution are captured.
Consent records policy version, timestamp and source context.
Lead list supports search, filter, sort and pagination.
Dashboard shows pipeline, new leads, follow-ups, conversion and sources.
next_follow_up_on is maintained from planned activities; overdue is highlighted.
Leads can be soft-deleted and restored by authorized users.
Leads can be exported to CSV (permission-gated, audited).
Public intake requires CAPTCHA (Turnstile) and rate limiting, plus a honeypot; blocks are security events.
If the API is unavailable, the website preserves the existing WhatsApp hand-off.
New and assigned leads notify permission-resolved recipients in-app and by email.
Quoted amount is recorded in minor units.
Auto-assignment (round robin).
Public form requires name, phone and consent; email, city, project_type, budget_range and message are optional.
Staff can enrich optional fields after capture.
The public API returns only a random public reference and a message; no lead id, number, status or internal field is exposed.
The public form has an accessible error state.
Users with access to a lead can add notes.
Authors edit and delete their own notes; ALL scope allows others.
Notes can be pinned.
Notes are INTERNAL; CUSTOMER_VISIBLE is reserved and rejected in P0.
Activities of type CALL, WHATSAPP, EMAIL, MEETING, SITE_VISIT, QUOTATION, FOLLOW_UP can be recorded.
Activities can be planned, completed or cancelled.
Completing an activity records outcome and time.
Status changes and assignments generate immutable system activities.
Call and WhatsApp buttons prompt a prefilled activity quick-log.
In-app notifications with unread count and mark-as-read.
Transactional email through a pluggable provider adapter.
Side effects go through a transactional outbox.
Outbox retries with backoff and dead-letters with alerting.
Email templates are versioned, branded, with plain-text alternatives.
Follow-up reminders and daily digest.
WhatsApp Business API notifications.
Email delivery failures never roll back or block a persisted lead.
Amazon SES in production; a development/test adapter elsewhere until SES production access exists.
Structured JSON application logs.
Every request has a request_id returned in headers and error bodies and present in logs, audit and security events.
Logs never contain passwords, tokens or unmasked personal data.
Unhandled exceptions are reported to an error tracker.
Health and readiness endpoints.
Metrics and alerting are mandatory in P0.
TLS end to end and HSTS.
CORS allow-list with credentials only for the app origin.
Strict security headers and CSP.
All input validated against closed schemas with length limits.
Secrets in AWS SSM, Secrets Manager or KMS with documented rotation.
The origin accepts traffic only from Cloudflare.
Dependency and container vulnerability scanning in CI.
Backups are encrypted and restore is verified automatically.
DPDP Act 2023 alignment.
Target OWASP ASVS v4 Level 2.
Rate limiting at edge and application for auth, MFA and public endpoints.
REST over HTTPS with JSON under /api/v1.
Standard success envelope.
Errors use RFC 9457 problem details with stable codes.
Offset pagination for admin lists and cursor pagination for streams.
Filtering, search and allow-listed sorting.
Updates require If-Match; stale versions return 409.
Idempotency-Key on creates, required for public intake.
OpenAPI 3.1 is the contract source of truth.
Only additive changes within v1; breaking changes require v2.
Login screen.
Forgot password and reset screens.
Lead dashboard.
Lead details.
Lead create and edit.
User management.
Role management.
Permission management.
Audit log viewer, including security events.
Visual language derives from Veda Spaces brand tokens.
WCAG 2.2 AA conformance.
Lead screens are fully usable at 360 px width.
UI hides or disables actions the user lacks permission for (cosmetic).
Accessibility corrections are encoded as design-system tokens.
MFA challenge, enrollment, recovery-code and step-up screens.
CI runs the full suite on SQLite and PostgreSQL.
Continuous SQLite replication to S3 plus nightly snapshots.
Local, staging and production environments; staging uses synthetic or anonymized data.
Migration runbook with pre-migration backup and rollback.
RPO and RTO are owner-approved values, measured in rehearsal.
Exactly one active application instance while SQLite is authoritative.
SQLite lives on a dedicated, persistent, encrypted volume, never only in a container layer.
PostgreSQL migration is a release gate before procurement, inventory, finance or multi-instance scale.
Automated restore verification with alerting.
p95 API latency below 300 ms for list and detail endpoints at the load-test fixture sizes (ASM-007).
API availability meets the owner-approved target (OWNER-INPUT-001).
Public intake p95 below 800 ms including CAPTCHA verification.
Initial JS below 200 KB gzipped and LCP below 2.5 s on 4G.
